title: Who Ordered?
story: Orders only store a customer_id number. Join the customers table to see real names next to each order date.
goal: Show each order's customer name and order_date (one row per order).

tests.label: Hidden check on other data
Hidden check on other data

hints: JOIN connects two tables where a condition matches: ON c.id = o.customer_id.
Give tables short nicknames: orders o, customers c.
SELECT c.name, o.order_date FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id;
socratic: Which column links an order to a customer?
Compare the rows you got with the rows expected. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what does your query do?
solution: SELECT c.name, o.order_date FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id;
alt: SELECT customers.name, orders.order_date FROM customers INNER JOIN orders ON orders.customer_id = customers.id;
